learningObjectives.title: Beliefs about God and the covenant

questions.q: Which prayer is the central declaration of Jewish faith, beginning 'Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is One'?
questions.explain: The Shema affirms belief in one God and is drawn from Deuteronomy 6:4.

questions.q: The Jewish belief that there is only one God is known as which of the following?
questions.explain: Judaism is monotheistic, teaching that there is one single, indivisible God.

questions.q: With which patriarch did God first make the covenant, promising many descendants and a land?
questions.explain: God made the first covenant with Abraham, the founding patriarch of the Jewish people.

questions.q: At which mountain did Moses receive the Torah and the Ten Commandments from God?
questions.explain: The covenant at Mount Sinai gave Israel the Torah, including the Ten Commandments.

questions.q: What physical sign marked the covenant between God and Abraham?
questions.explain: Circumcision of male children became the outward sign of the Abrahamic covenant.

questions.q: The Ten Commandments given at Sinai are also known by which term?
questions.explain: 'Decalogue' means 'ten words' and is another name for the Ten Commandments.

questions.q: Jews describe God as 'omnipotent'. What does this mean?
questions.explain: Omnipotent means God has unlimited power, as shown in creating the world.

questions.q: Which Hebrew term for the synagogue means 'house of assembly'?
questions.explain: 'Beit Knesset' means house of assembly, reflecting the synagogue's role as a gathering place.

questions.q: What is the name of the cabinet in the synagogue that holds the Torah scrolls?
questions.explain: The Aron Hakodesh, or Holy Ark, stores the Torah scrolls and usually faces Jerusalem.

questions.q: The Ner Tamid, or 'eternal light', hangs above the Ark. What does it symbolise?
questions.explain: The ever-burning Ner Tamid represents God's constant and eternal presence.

questions.q: Where are tefillin worn by many Jews during weekday morning prayers?
questions.explain: Tefillin are small boxes containing scripture, bound on the arm and forehead in obedience to the Shema.

questions.q: What is a 'minyan' in Jewish worship?
options: The quorum of ten adults required for communal prayer
The prayer book used in services
The raised platform for reading the Torah
questions.explain: A minyan of ten adults is traditionally needed before certain public prayers can be said.

questions.q: On Friday evening a Jewish family lights two candles, blesses wine and shares challah bread. Which observance are they beginning?
questions.explain: Shabbat, the weekly day of rest, begins at sunset on Friday with candles, wine and challah.

questions.q: Which instrument, made from a ram's horn, is blown during Rosh Hashanah?
questions.explain: The shofar is sounded at Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish New Year, calling people to repentance.

questions.q: Yom Kippur is the holiest day of the Jewish year. By what name is it also known?
questions.explain: On Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement, Jews fast and seek forgiveness for their sins.

questions.q: What historical event does the festival of Pesach (Passover) commemorate?
options: The Exodus of the Israelites from slavery in Egypt
The giving of the Torah at Sinai
questions.explain: Pesach recalls the Israelites' escape from slavery in Egypt under Moses.

questions.q: At how many days old is a Jewish baby boy traditionally circumcised in the Brit Milah?
questions.explain: Brit Milah takes place on the eighth day after birth, following the command given to Abraham.

questions.q: A thirteen-year-old boy is called up to read from the Torah in the synagogue for the first time and becomes responsible for keeping the commandments. Which rite of passage is this?
questions.explain: At thirteen a boy becomes bar mitzvah, 'son of the commandment', taking on adult religious duties.

questions.q: A family gathers for a ritual meal, reads the Haggadah and eats matzah (unleavened bread) to remember their ancestors' escape from Egypt. Which festival are they celebrating?
questions.explain: The Seder meal at Pesach uses the Haggadah and matzah to retell the Exodus story.

questions.q: A couple stand beneath a canopy (chuppah) and the ceremony ends with the groom breaking a glass underfoot. Which rite of passage is taking place?
questions.explain: Jewish weddings are held under a chuppah and traditionally end with the breaking of a glass.
